sections.h2: Where is the Putnam County Register of Deeds and what does it do?
sections.html:
The office sits in Room 3 of the Putnam County Courthouse at 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501. It is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and the phone is 931-526-7101. The county site lists John Sanders as Register.

This office records land deeds, mortgages, releases, plats, powers of attorney and liens, including judgment liens, materialman's liens and state and federal tax liens. The county says its records reach back to 1854, the year Putnam County was re-established after an earlier version was dissolved by the courts. Anyone can ask for a copy of a recorded document in person, by phone, by mail or by email, except military discharge papers (DD-214), which are not public.

The staff will help work out a fee, but they cannot draft a deed for you. If you sell a Putnam County house, a title company or attorney normally prepares the deed, and the register records it once the tax is paid.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Putnam County?
sections.html:
The county's fee schedule charges by the thousand dollars for deeds and trust deeds, plus per-page and flat fees. Documents filed electronically carry an extra $2.00 fee, in place since July 1, 2023.

DocumentFee listed by the county
Warranty deed$3.70 per thousand, $5.00 per page (2 page minimum), $1.00 clerk fee, $2.00 EDP fee
Trust deed (mortgage)$1.15 per thousand after the first $2,000, plus the same page, clerk and EDP fees
ModificationCharged like a trust deed, with no $2,000 deduction
Release$10.00 plus $2.00 EDP fee, $5.00 for each extra reference
Other documents$5.00 per page (2 page minimum), $5.00 for each added page, plus $2.00 EDP fee
Fixture filing$13.00 plus $2.00 EDP fee, $15.00 for each added name
DD-214 dischargeFree

Source: Putnam County Register of Deeds, Recording/Filing Fees. Call 931-526-7101 if your paperwork has odd attachments, since page counts move the total.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Putnam County home sale?
sections.html:
Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100, and the state Department of Revenue describes the base as the purchase price. Its help desk adds that the tax generally uses the greater of the price paid or the property's value, under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409. The county's warranty deed line of $3.70 per thousand is the same rate written another way.

Here is a worked case. The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $282,500 in Putnam County for 2020 to 2024. On a sale at that figure, the transfer tax is 2,825 hundreds times $0.37, or $1,045.25. Add the page fees ($10 for two pages), the $1.00 clerk fee and the $2.00 EDP fee, and the deed costs $1,058.25 to record.

A buyer who finances $225,000 also pays the indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000, which is $256.45. Recording the trust deed brings that to $269.45 with the same flat fees. The purchase contract and your title agent will say who carries each charge.

sections.h2: What must a document include to be recorded in Putnam County?
sections.html:
The register lists seven requirements. A document that misses one will not be accepted at the counter.

  • It must be the original or a certified copy.
  • It must state who prepared it.
  • The grantor and grantee must be named.
  • The date of signing must appear.
  • A deed must carry an Oath of Consideration.
  • A deed of trust must state the maximum principal indebtedness.
  • A notary statement and notary seal must be present.

The oath matters because the tax is based on it. Fill in the real price or value, and let the title agent review the figure before anyone signs.

sections.h2: How do you research a property or guard against deed fraud in Putnam County?
sections.html:
You can search records in person at the courthouse, or online through US Title Search, which charges a monthly fee. The office can also look up the year a house was built from its tax card, and the Assessor's Office holds the same detail.

The register promotes My Land Alert, a free service at mylandalert.com that sends an email when a document is recorded in your name or your business name. Owners who rent out a house or live elsewhere should consider it. An alert gives you days, not years, to spot a deed you did not sign.

sections.h2: How do you change or correct a deed in Putnam County?
sections.html:
You cannot edit a recorded deed at the counter. To add or remove a name, you need a new deed prepared by an attorney or title agency, then recorded with the proper oath and fees.

Owners may write their own deed under Putnam County's FAQ, but the register does not recommend it and cannot help prepare one. A homemade deed that omits a required line gets turned away, and that can hold up a closing. When a mortgage is paid off, the lender sends the release to the register, and you can ask for a copy once it is recorded.

sections.h2: How did Putnam County get its shape?
sections.html:
The state first created the county in 1842 from parts of Jackson, Overton, Fentress and White counties. Overton and Jackson counties won an injunction, and a chancellor dissolved Putnam in 1845 because the new county cut their areas below constitutional limits. The legislature re-established it in 1854, and the act named the county town Cookeville for Richard F. Cooke, a state senator.

White Plains, near modern Algood, served as the temporary seat. The county is named for Israel Putnam, a general of the Revolutionary War. Caves in the Calfkiller Valley held saltpeter mines in the War of 1812 and the Civil War. Water leaves the county by three routes: tributaries of the Caney Fork in the south, the Obey River in the northeast, and Cordell Hull Lake in the north and west. Burgess Falls sits near the White County line.

The register's books start in 1854, so a title agent can trace a Putnam County parcel back to the year the county was re-established.

sections.h2: What shapes house sales around Cookeville and the rest of Putnam County?
sections.html:
Putnam County covers 403 square miles and runs on Central Time. Seven counties touch it: Overton, Fentress, Cumberland, White, DeKalb, Smith and Jackson. Cookeville is the county seat and the largest city, and Algood is the other city. Baxter and Monterey are towns. A deed for a house in any of them goes to the same courthouse office.

Tennessee Technological University is in Cookeville, and the student body is reported at about 11,800. The Census Bureau puts the county at 86,612 people on July 1, 2025, up 8.4 percent from the 2020 base. It counts 38,375 housing units, a 61.2 percent owner-occupancy rate, a median rent of $908 and a median household income of $58,912. Builders took out 629 permits in 2025. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,450, and owners without one report $446. The county counts 4,146 veterans, which is one reason the free DD-214 filing exists.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a warranty deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: The county charges $3.70 per thousand dollars of value, $5.00 per page with a two-page minimum, a $1.00 clerk fee and a $2.00 EDP fee. On a $282,500 sale that totals $1,058.25 for a two-page deed.

faqs.q: Who is the Putnam County Register of Deeds and where is the office?
faqs.a: John Sanders is listed as Register. The office is in Room 3 of the Putnam County Courthouse, 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501, and the number is 931-526-7101.

faqs.q: Do I need an Oath of Consideration to record a deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's checklist says deeds must include an Oath of Consideration, and deeds of trust must state the maximum principal indebtedness.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of someone else's deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: Yes. Every recorded document is public except DD-214 discharge papers, and you can request copies in person, by phone, by mail or by email.

faqs.q: Can I add or remove a name on my Putnam County deed myself?
faqs.a: A new deed is required, and the register says an attorney or title agency should prepare it. The office cannot help write the deed and does not recommend doing it yourself.
